projects.title: ClickDrobe
projects.description: A cross-platform Flutter app that turns clothing photos and share-sheet imports into structured wardrobe items using Gemini vision, then handles outfit planning, wear tracking, and personalized styling. Underneath it runs an asynchronous PostgreSQL ingestion pipeline — row-level locking, event-driven workers, recovery sweeps — processing roughly 15–30 garments a minute with 73% fewer worker invocations. Invalid outfit combinations turned out to trace back to free-text garment labels, so the whole system now shares one canonical taxonomy across ingestion, recommendations, backfills, and evaluation tooling.

projects.title: AlgoView
projects.description: A browser-based teaching platform that visualizes 19 algorithms across five categories. Execution-state snapshots make a run fully scrubbable — play, pause, step backward — with pseudocode and complexity analysis staying in sync. A separate benchmarking engine runs the real sorting implementations in background workers across varying input sizes and plots the empirical runtime curve against the theoretical Big-O, all without blocking the interface.

experience.description: Supported 200+ graduate students across two semesters of Programming Design Paradigm and Algorithms — office hours, technical activities, code reviews, grading, and one-on-one debugging. Most of the mentoring landed on Java, data structures, algorithm design, and software architecture.

Optimized Java/Spring Boot microservices for a telecom client's backend handling 5,000+ daily requests — query caching and load balancing cut API response times 20% (500ms → 400ms). Automated build and deployment workflows with Docker and Jenkins, pulling the release cycle from four weeks to three across three microservices. Restructured queries and added targeted indexes on internal simulation tools for a 30% drop in execution time (1,000ms → 700ms).

Built and shipped a cross-platform inventory app (Flutter, Firestore) onto shop-floor devices, replacing paper-based stock logging and cutting processing errors by 50%. Real-time raw-materials tracking with Firestore sync reduced material wastage 42% — an estimated $15K a year. Automated reporting (Cloud Scheduler → Cloud Functions) produced daily consumption, wastage, and stock-valuation summaries as PDF/CSV, saving five hours a week of manual reconciliation.
